The complete curriculum is reproduced below at its regulated component-credit level. The two faculty-wide modules preserve their regulated choice between Global Change and Cultural Heritage, and the 30-EC minor remains genuine open minor space. No formal route is defined.

programmes.label: Middle Eastern Studies at University of Groningen

exception.reason: The University of Groningen programme is an integrated area-studies degree anchored in a progressive 30-EC Arabic-language sequence and a compulsory 30-EC study-abroad semester in Cairo or Rabat. Its disciplinary spine then studies the modern Middle East through region-specific history, Judaism and Islam, politics and international relations, culture and soft power, empire and colonialism, Islam and modernity, conflict, and relations between Europe and the Middle East. UCR offers meaningful global history, empire, international relations, peace and conflict, public international law, migration, sociology, literature, media and cultural-heritage courses. It offers neither Arabic nor a Middle Eastern Studies, Islam, Judaism or regional religious-studies sequence, and it has no embedded regional semester equivalent. A UCR programme built from the closest courses would be a credible global-history or international-relations pathway, but not a defensible Middle Eastern Studies comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 regulations account for the full 180 EC. Year one combines 20 EC of beginner and intermediate Arabic with modern Middle Eastern history, Judaism and Islam, academic debates in Middle Eastern Studies, politics and international relations, specialist writing, and a 10-EC faculty-wide module. Year two combines 10 EC of advanced Arabic, 20 EC on culture and soft power, Jews and Muslims under empire and colonialism, and Islam, politics and modernity, followed by a compulsory 30-EC study-abroad programme in Cairo or Rabat. Year three comprises a 30-EC minor, a 10-EC thesis, a second 10-EC faculty-wide module, and courses on contemporary conflict and Europe-Middle East relations. The live programme page likewise emphasizes the modern Middle East and North Africa, Arabic as a world language, regional politics and current affairs, cultural diversity, and the semester abroad.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict and GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law provide relevant foundations in modern history, imperialism, international relations, conflict, refugee law, self-determination and postcolonial legal critique. GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Sociology of Development and GOSSOCI311 Social Change & Civil Society address colonialism, the Global South, migration, development and civil society. HCBPSYC315 Youth Resilience to Extremism examines radicalisation and prevention. MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage, MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & the Global Mediterranean and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature add cultural and literary perspectives, including Mediterranean exchange and some Arabic literature; UCR's media and communication courses can support analysis of representation and public communication. The workbook nevertheless contains no Arabic-language course at any level, no Middle Eastern history or area-studies sequence, no Islam or Judaism course, no sustained study of Middle Eastern politics, culture and society, and no embedded Cairo- or Rabat-based semester. Scattered global and comparative courses therefore cannot reproduce the programme's combined Arabic, region-specific humanities and social-science formation or its mandatory regional immersion.
